dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The suspicious May batch consists of 17 annual renewals posted on 31 May: 8 from DLR-104 totalling $723.42 and 9 from DLR-219 totalling $782.87, for $1,506.29 combined."

"Both 31-May import files reconcile exactly: DF-00020 has 8 received = 8 accepted, $723.42 source/ledger total and zero reconciliation difference; DF-00040 has 9 = 9, $782.87 source/ledger total and zero difference."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The effective transaction dates are not concentrated on 31 May... indicating earlier events posted together at month-end."

"Operations' explanation that dealer annual-plan files retain the transaction date as effective_event_date but are posted at month-end is consistent with the independently observed data and reconciliation controls."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"The data does not establish why the posting regime appears to shift from daily posting in Jan–Feb to month-end batching from March."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or suppress the 31-May revenue."
"For weekly/trend reporting, use effective_event_date for these dealer annual renewals, or annotate month-end batches separately so posting mechanics do not create an artificial spike."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material revenue issue. Confidence: High."
"Separately confirm the dealer contract/configuration effective date and clarify whether cash_total_usd intentionally includes dealer-originated UPI transactions."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The underlying economic events appear distinct and reconciled" is somewhat stronger than the evidence presented because the submission does not demonstrate an entitlement-level reconciliation or independently establish that every effective date represents a genuine economic event.

"There is no duplicate-event evidence" is well supported for duplicate recharge IDs, source_event_ids, and exact rows, but does not by itself rule out duplicate downstream entitlements or ledger postings.

"Material pipeline defect: Rejected for the revenue question because no lost/extra rows or reconciliation differences are present" narrows the conclusion appropriately for revenue, but accepted-row and file-total checks do not fully exclude other pipeline defects affecting downstream analytics.

"The 31-May West annual-renewal spike is best explained by month-end batching of genuine dealer renewals" is plausible and corroborated, but the dealer email and effective dates do not independently prove the underlying business events were genuine.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a basic import-failure interpretation, but missed or did not test the strongest residual alternative: duplicate or inconsistent downstream entitlement creation despite clean source-file counts and ledger-total reconciliation. A secondary alternative is a configuration or metadata defect that preserves source totals while distorting event-time analytics.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and explicitly report an entitlement-level join/reconciliation for the 17 affected source_event_ids—checking one-to-one mapping, entitlement counts, and duplicate downstream postings—before assigning high confidence to the no-material-issue conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "In equal 52-day windows, South tickets fell 318→196 (-38.4%), while non-South controls rose 707→746 (+5.5%)."
"At authenticate alone there were 302 ERROR and 162 ABANDONED sessions."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "NovaIVR also changes which journeys become CareDesk cases."
"The data supports fewer recorded cases and transfers, not yet the causal claim that customers experienced fewer or better-resolved problems."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "‘NovaIVR clearly harmed customers’ — also rejected. It recorded 1,521 resolved sessions and absolute transfers declined, so genuine benefit is plausible."

"Material unknowns are whether logging/traffic coverage changed at cutover, what RESOLVED guarantees, whether failed users recontacted elsewhere, why non-IVR ticket origins also fell, and whether South-specific case-entry policies changed."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not treat the South complaint decline as sufficient evidence that NovaIVR improved customer experience, and do not expand nationally yet."
"Keep the South pilot only; neither roll back nor expand nationally yet. Instrument pre-authentication failures and link journeys to repeat contacts where permitted."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Evaluate stable measures such as contacts per active subscriber, repeat-contact rate, verified resolution, error/abandonment rate, transfers per eligible contact and sampled-call/CSAT outcomes."
"What exact condition causes a NovaIVR interaction to be labelled RESOLVED, and what evidence validates that the 1,521 RESOLVED sessions actually solved the customer's issue?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claims are evident. The statement that "NovaIVR also changes which journeys become CareDesk cases" is appropriately supported by the cited email and interaction data, though the extent of the change remains unknown.

The phrase "NovaIVR clearly harmed customers — also rejected" is properly presented as a rejected hypothesis, not as a factual claim; absolute transfer decline alone would not establish genuine benefit, but the submission explicitly treats benefit only as plausible.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest alternative: NovaIVR may have produced genuine self-service benefit, as suggested by 1,521 RESOLVED sessions and lower absolute transfers, while also creating a measurement boundary. It also preserved the alternative that non-IVR routing, staffing, population, or case-entry changes explain part of the decline.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quantify end-to-end outcomes by linking every pre-authentication ERROR or ABANDONED journey to repeat IVR attempts, agent/app/dealer contacts, CareDesk cases, and verified resolution within 24 and 72 hours, with a comparable pre-pilot cohort.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` for the four unique events, clearance status, durations, severity mix, duplicate count, and zero `impact_mw`.

It explicitly distinguishes the observed zero values from the inference that they might reflect an export/default convention: "That may be genuinely zero impact, but... it could also be an export/default-value convention."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It uses several event attributes together rather than relying on wording alone: "no positive MW impact, persistent uncleared event, critical severity, duplicate/repeating event."

It identifies a plausible innocent explanation for the zero-impact field and proposes checking a raw/source record, but it does not itself triangulate against an independent channel in the submission.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission assigns claim-specific confidence, using High for directly observed CSV properties and Medium for the data-quality concern.
It states the limitation that `TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED` does not prove a failure because "the preceding history is outside this tiny extract," and identifies the smallest decision-changing check.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate: "Perform one cheap check, then stop unless it fails."
The proposed validation of `impact_mw` against raw/source telemetry or its field definition is discriminating and preserves escalation only if the check contradicts the export.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion appropriately avoids inferring equipment failure from four short, cleared events with reported zero MW impact.
It matches the evidence-supported stopping point: "If zero is confirmed, there is insufficient evidence here to justify escalation."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that no operational pattern "currently warrants escalation" is an inference rather than a directly observed fact, though it is appropriately supported by the cited event attributes and scoped to the extract.
The possibility that `impact_mw=0` is an export/default convention is unverified, but it is presented as a hypothesis and not asserted as fact.
The submission says the sample has "0 duplicate rows" while the evidence table summarizes this as no duplicate event keys; this is a minor wording ambiguity, not a material overstatement.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The zero-impact values could be a systematic export or default-value artifact, meaning the short cleared durations and benign-looking event metadata might understate actual production impact. The proposed raw-record/field-definition check is the right way to discriminate this alternative without inventing a plant problem.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Actually perform the proposed cross-channel validation of `impact_mw` for INV-17, including the field definition or raw telemetry, and record whether zero represents measured impact or a default/export convention.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` and the impact note for the exact daily penalties, ₹662,444.09 and ₹453,085.88, and the 31.60% calculation.
It explicitly distinguishes the observed comparison from causality: “the evidence does not establish that the pilot causally reduced DSM penalty by exactly 31.6%.”
The same-day counterfactual is tied to 29-May base versus submitted schedules and reports the resulting ₹549,664.38 versus ₹453,085.88 penalties.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission checks an innocent operating-day explanation using measured wind, gust, availability, stow count, curtailment and cloud factor rather than treating the headline comparison as self-proving.
It triangulates daily settlement totals, block-level schedule differences, absolute generation gaps and the commercial extract.
It correctly identifies remaining confounders: “unmeasured forecast difficulty, base-schedule quality, operator decisions or other day-specific factors may differ.”

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It gives claim-specific confidence, rating arithmetic reproducibility high while rating the same-day calculation medium-high and explicitly limiting causal interpretation.
It states that the 17.57% result is “a useful mechanical counterfactual, not full causal proof” because it assumes realised generation would have been unchanged.
It proposes prospective paired data and, where safe, randomisation as the smallest meaningful evidence improvement.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation preserves operational caution: “Continue the pilot in its current limited scope,” while rejecting broad expansion based on one comparison.
It recommends a pre-specified shadow comparison using both schedules against the same realised meter data and repeated high-wind days.

It retains the legitimate observed benefit by reporting both the 31.6% day-to-day comparison and the 17.57% same-day mechanical result without presenting either as established causal treatment effect.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion directly satisfies the central distinction between “pilot day performed better” and “pilot caused 31.6% reduction.”
It keeps a narrower positive finding—“the pilot revisions were directionally beneficial on the realised 29-May blocks”—rather than overcorrecting to no value.
It accurately concludes that the 31.6% figure is reproducible but not identified as a causal estimate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “28 and 29 May appear operationally similar” is reasonable for the listed measured variables, but it could be read too broadly because those variables do not establish similarity in forecast difficulty, market conditions, operator behavior or other unmeasured drivers.

“The pilot revisions were directionally beneficial” is appropriately narrowed to realised blocks, but remains a mechanical schedule-versus-base comparison rather than evidence that the revisions improved operational outcomes under an unchanged counterfactual.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction may reflect favorable day-specific conditions or differences in forecast and operator decisions, while the smaller 17.57% same-day mechanical result indicates genuine schedule-value potential without identifying its causal operational effect.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed prospective paired shadow test across multiple eligible high-wind days, preserving both base and AI schedules before outcomes are known and evaluating both against identical realised meter data; randomise submission where operationally safe.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties claims to named files, including "`declaration.pdf`; `commercial_invoice.pdf`", "`country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`", and "`product_master_current.xlsx`".
It identifies specific fields and dates such as "2025-11-04", "90211000", "effective 2025-01-01", and "snapshot is 2025-12-31".
A minor limitation is that it provides no page, row, cell, or quoted source excerpts, so the cited evidence is traceable to files but not fully auditable at the passage level.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests and rejects the hypothesis that "90211000 vs 90211090 proves broker miscoding".
It separately rejects the hypothesis that "The current Helios value proves what Switzerland should have used on 4 Nov".
It identifies a decisive competing test: "an authoritative Swiss Tares classification or product-specific ruling applicable to P1001 on 2025-11-04".

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion states "Confidence: High" while limiting that confidence to the explanation that the mismatch reflects "different classification contexts".
It expressly qualifies accepted status: "The declaration's `Accepted` status is corroborative but does not itself prove legal correctness."
It identifies the precise uncertainty and escalation trigger: "If that required 90211090 or another code, I would escalate the declaration."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the mechanism as a context mismatch: "the Swiss declaration uses `90211000`, while the current Helios master contains `90211090`."
It identifies a data-model limitation: the canonical schema "does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates or ruling authority."

It gives a sound control implication: "Future comparisons should use jurisdiction-specific, effective-dated classifications rather than directly comparing the canonical eight-character field with current Helios."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended action is proportionate and reversible: "Suppress this declaration-error alert pending a cheap Swiss-authority check and open a control-fix ticket."
It avoids an unsupported amendment: "Do not amend the accepted declaration unless the Swiss check conflicts with 90211000."
It preserves escalation if authoritative evidence changes the assessment: "If that required 90211090 or another code, I would escalate the declaration."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Confidence: High" is reasonable for the benign-mismatch explanation but is not independently demonstrated with quoted rows or authoritative ruling evidence; the submission appropriately limits legal correctness pending a Swiss check.
The characterization of the authority check as "cheap" is unsupported by evidence, though it does not materially affect the decision.
The claim that the Swiss matrix "independently supports 90211000" is plausible and properly sourced to the matrix, but would be stronger with the exact row and effective-date passage.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The declaration could still contain a classification error if an authoritative Swiss Tares decision or product-specific ruling applicable to P1001 on 2025-11-04 required 90211090 or another code. The submission identifies this alternative and specifies the evidence that would resolve it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add exact page, row, cell, or quoted excerpts from the declaration, Swiss matrix, product-master Read Me, and schema, especially the P1001 effective-date row and the Swiss nomenclature statement.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declaration IE-2025-000411 dated 2025-09-18 declares P1006, origin United States, and Preference = Yes; the invoice independently shows P1006 manufactured in the United States." Sources: `declaration.pdf`; `commercial_invoice.pdf`.
"The SUP-02/P1006 register entry is valid only through 2025-07-31, has status Expired in register, and therefore does not support the September declaration." Source: `supplier_origin_register.csv`.
"The packet contains no actual supplier declaration." Sources: `packet_manifest.txt`; `origin-workshop.md`.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Manufacturing origin is not evidence that preferential-origin requirements were satisfied."
"No current register record proves the claim is false — rejected."
"The expired SUP-02/P1006 record supports this filing — rejected."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Confidence: High on evidentiary insufficiency; Medium on whether the underlying claim is actually invalid."
"The missing/expired support warrants verification, but does not prove the preference claim is false."
"Do not conclude fraud or amend the accepted declaration solely because ClearView/register linkage is missing."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The workshop states that the register is not always updated when sourcing routes change, so support could exist outside it."
"declarations may exist in category folders even when the register is stale."
"retrieve the underlying supplier declaration and rule basis from the Procurement/category folder or broker."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place the preference claim on evidence hold and retrieve the underlying supplier declaration and rule basis from the Procurement/category folder or broker."
"Verify supplier, product, validity period and origin-rule coverage before clearing the claim."
"escalate for customs correction only if the retrieved evidence fails to support the claim."

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preferential-origin claim may be valid despite the expired register entry because a current supplier declaration and applicable rule evidence may exist in Procurement/category folders or with the broker; the available evidence establishes an evidentiary gap, not falsity. The US manufacturing information supports manufacturing country only and cannot independently establish preferential origin.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or identify the exact relevant fields and passages from each cited source, especially the invoice manufacturing-country field, the register search result, and the workshop's rule distinguishing manufacturing country from preferential origin.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The extract contains 262 batches; among 220 rows with release timing, median receipt→release is 39.40 h.” — Specific file, row counts, fields, and calculated result make the primary observation traceable.

“185 qcore_release_ts values occur exactly at 02:10” and “Upstream snapshots also differ materially in freshness” — The submission triangulates batch data with source_freshness and acknowledges relevant counterevidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “It measures the wrong starting point; receipt can precede completion of required evidence.” — Separates the observed symptom from the SOP mechanism.
“Laboratory completion does not establish certificate availability or exception resolution.” — Tests and rejects a plausible proxy rather than treating lab completion as the causal boundary.

“obtain (1) the timestamp when the last required evidence item became available, and (2) the actual QCore disposition/audit timestamp.” — Identifies observations that discriminate workflow delay from timestamp/interface effects.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “Confidence: High” is attached to the decision not to build the KPI, while the timestamp finding is labeled “Medium-High.” — Confidence is claim-specific rather than uniformly asserted.
“these cannot be classified as SLA breaches without knowing when the remaining required evidence became available.” — Missing evidence and source semantics materially constrain the conclusion.
“If the extract fields are shown to reliably represent those two events... If not...” — The recommendation changes according to the verification result.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Do not build the proposed cycle-time KPI from this extract yet.” — Reframes the task from calculating a potentially invalid KPI to validating its event definition.
“Perform a small timestamp-lineage check first.” — Proposes a bounded, reversible action that protects against optimizing a measurement artifact.
“If not, add the missing evidence-ready timestamp or correct the QCore timestamp lineage before publishing a performance KPI.” — Provides a practical safeguard and clear decision consequence.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “The 35–39 h median proves routine QC is missing its 24-h target — rejected.” — Rejects the strongest operational interpretation using the SOP clock definition.
“Using lab completion fixes the KPI — rejected.” — Tests a second plausible alternative and explains the missing certificate/exception timestamps.
“If the extract fields are shown to reliably represent those two events, build the dashboard...” — States what future evidence could revive the KPI interpretation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “trace 5–10 routine released batches” — Requests a small, high-value sample rather than all data.

“For each, obtain ... the timestamp when the last required evidence item became available, and ... the actual QCore disposition/audit timestamp.” — Directly targets the two unresolved event definitions and their decision impact.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The “routine-like subset” is not formally defined in the submission, so the 34.97 h statistic is not independently auditable from the text alone; this does not materially weaken the primary conclusion because the SOP-clock mismatch remains established.

The phrase “snapshots ... differ materially in freshness” is supported by the cited dates but does not by itself prove that any particular row-level status conflict is caused by temporal inconsistency; the submission appropriately treats this as a reason for verification rather than a settled cause.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A genuine post-evidence operational delay may still exist: if the last required-evidence timestamp precedes the QCore disposition/audit timestamp by more than 24 hours, the KPI could reveal a real SLA problem. The current extract cannot distinguish that from interface-commit timing and non-coherent source snapshots.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the verification explicitly reconcile source snapshots and event identity for the sampled batches: obtain the last-required-evidence event, QCore audit/decision event, extract timestamps, and source snapshot times in one comparison so that both workflow delay and timestamp-lineage explanations can be separated.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Some strong semantic hits are blocked: MTR-4401 stock is reserved/zero-free for the required revisions, while VLV-3722 Rev-A requests have only Rev-B catalogue stock." — cites spare_parts.csv and part_restrictions.csv; this is specific and cross-file traceable.
"Global stock is not sufficiently current... MaintStar-global snapshot is 2026-06-26, while local restriction status is 2026-07-30" — cites source_freshness.csv and maintenance_email.txt.
The dollar totals ($166,495.60 and $47,257) and the 28.4% calculation are asserted without a row-level calculation, field references, or reconciliation to the 24 requests.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Every semantic hit represents avoidable purchase value" — rejected using revision mismatch, critical reservations, insufficient quantity, and site qualification as blocking mechanisms.
"The same physical donor unit cannot satisfy multiple open requests" — rejected independent summation and explains why candidate value differs from realizable value.

The reasoning appropriately separates semantic retrieval from transferability, though it does not fully test whether each numerical match remains valid after all restrictions and freshness issues are applied.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "I am prepared to call 0% actionable now from these extracts" and "Needs check" preserve an important distinction between current evidence and verified actionability.
"At most about $47,257 (28.4%) has a plausible cross-site candidate worth engineering/live-stock verification" bounds candidate value rather than presenting it as savings.

The high-confidence framing is somewhat stronger than the evidence supports for the zero-actionability conclusion, because stale global data creates uncertainty rather than proving that no transfer is currently possible.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Recommendation: pilot semantic search for candidate discovery and prioritisation, but keep engineering and live-stock validation as mandatory gates before cancelling or avoiding an external purchase."
The recommendation is reversible, operationally safe, and directly reframes semantic search from an automatic transfer or savings engine into a controlled candidate-generation tool.
The proposed live donor-site check and receiving-engineer confirmation create a practical next iteration and protect against reservation, revision, qualification, and availability risks.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects three plausible alternatives: treating every semantic hit as avoidable value, independently summing global stock, and assuming that different wording means no opportunity.
It identifies evidence that would revive or reduce the candidate opportunity: live stock, reservation status, engineering equivalence, revision/configuration, UOM, and qualification checks.
The competing explanation that stale global data may conceal currently usable local stock is acknowledged but not explicitly framed as a hypothesis with a quantified impact.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "For the shortlisted matches, query the live donor-site CMMS for current unreserved quantity and reservation/critical-spare status" and obtain receiving-engineer confirmation of MPN, revision/configuration, UOM, and qualification.
This is a focused, high-value evidence request tied directly to the decision gate rather than a generic request for more data.
It could be more prioritized by naming the first donor/request pair or the minimum fields and freshness threshold needed to validate the highest-value candidate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "I am prepared to call 0% actionable now" is defensible as a decision from the provided extracts, but it is overstated if interpreted as evidence that no transfer is currently possible; the stale global snapshot mainly means actionability is unverified.

The $166,495.60 apparent external-purchase value, $47,257 candidate value, and 28.4% share are not supported by a visible row-level calculation or explicit allocation of each request, donor quantity, and purchase amount.
The table's "matching free cross-site stock" for PLC-8840 and the aggregate candidate classification need more specific part, site, quantity, and restriction evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search pilot may identify materially more actionable value than the reported 28.4% ceiling because the MaintStar global extract is older than local restriction data; some apparently unavailable or reserved stock could be usable after a current donor-site CMMS check. Conversely, the candidate amount could fall further once engineering equivalence and site qualification are confirmed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a row-level reconciliation for all 24 requests showing request quantity and value, exact MPN/revision/UOM, donor site and free quantity, restriction/qualification status, donor-unit allocation, and the formula producing the $166,495.60 and $47,257 totals; then validate the highest-value donor candidates against live CMMS data.
